policy_title: Replace the 2010 Equalities Act and scrap DE&I rules
stated: Reform UK will replace the 2010 Equalities Act, stating it requires discrimination in the name of 'positive action,' and will scrap Diversity, Equality and Inclusion (DE&I) rules that they claim have lowered standards and reduced economic productivity.

source.quote: Replace the 2010 Equalities Act The Equalities Act requires discrimination in the name of ‘positive action’. We will scrap Diversity, Equality and Inclusion (DE&I) rules that have lowered standards and reduced economic productivity.

bearing_set.reason: Replacing the Equality Act directly removes or rewrites statutory anti-discrimination protections and equal-treatment rights for people with protected characteristics — core O9 territory.

The Equality Act's employment provisions (equal pay, protection from workplace discrimination, gender pay gap reporting) and DE&I hiring rules directly affect pay equity, employment rights, and job security for protected groups — a real verdict on fair pay and work quality.

Equal-pay and employment-discrimination protections concretely narrow wage and employment gaps by protected characteristic; removing them has a specific mechanism by which income inequality between groups plausibly widens.

The policy's explicit stated rationale is that DE&I rules have reduced economic productivity and lowered standards — a genuinely contested empirical claim about aggregate living standards that earns a real verdict.

Mandatory public-sector equality duties, compulsory DE&I reporting, and mandated training represent state coercion on employers and institutions; scrapping them removes those mandates, a concrete O10 mechanism.

membership_note: This is a sweeping legislative replacement, not a narrow measure: it touches equal-treatment law (O9), workplace rights and pay equity (O4), distributional inequality (O14), aggregate productivity claims (O13), and removal of state mandates (O10). Five bearings are warranted given the policy's scope.
